disease_label_per_paper: Right upper quadrant presentation of acute diverticulitis
presentation_summary: 27-year-old woman presented with two days of severe epigastric and right upper quadrant abdominal pain rated 10/10, sharp, and extending to the back.
Symptoms included nausea, reduced appetite, headache, chills, and night sweats; she denied subjective fever but measured temperature was 39.1 C.
Exam showed epigastric and right upper quadrant tenderness.
Laboratory testing showed leukocytosis of 21,460/uL with left shift; lipase, kidney function, and liver function tests were reported normal.

CT abdomen and pelvis showed diverticulosis of the ascending colon, transverse colon, and hepatic flexure with hepatic-flexure wall thickening and pericolic fat stranding suggestive of acute diverticulitis.
